description: Table 4 is a plain two-row data table (no image panels, no axes, no scale bars) reporting the quantitative chemical compositions in wt% of the austenite phase in two Nb-containing medium-Mn low-density steels. The header row lists the column keys "Samples", "Mn", "Al", "Cr", "C", "Nb" and "Fe". The first data row, "0.02Nb steel", gives Mn 13.12, Al 8.35, Cr 4.06, C 1.39, Nb 0.019 and Fe 63.79 wt%. The second data row, "0.04Nb steel", gives Mn 13.03, Al 8.37, Cr 3.97, C 1.33, Nb 0.038 and Fe 64.07 wt%. The only substantial difference between the two steels is the Nb content, which roughly doubles from 0.019 to 0.038 wt%; Al (8.35 vs 8.37), C (1.39 vs 1.33), Mn (13.12 vs 13.03), Cr (4.06 vs 3.97) and Fe (63.79 vs 64.07) are essentially unchanged. Values sum to about 90.7 wt% for the 0.02Nb steel and 90.8 wt% for the 0.04Nb steel, indicating the reported elements do not account for the whole composition. The table's role is to demonstrate that doubling the Nb addition leaves the austenite chemistry — in particular the κ-carbide-forming elements Al and C — essentially constant.

observations.observation: The table's column headers are 'Samples', 'Mn', 'Al', 'Cr', 'C', 'Nb' and 'Fe', with two data rows labelled '0.02Nb steel' and '0.04Nb steel'.
Austenite in the 0.02Nb steel contains Mn 13.12, Al 8.35, Cr 4.06, C 1.39, Nb 0.019 and Fe 63.79 wt%.
Austenite in the 0.04Nb steel contains Mn 13.03, Al 8.37, Cr 3.97, C 1.33, Nb 0.038 and Fe 64.07 wt%.
The Nb content of austenite roughly doubles between the two steels, from 0.019 wt% (0.02Nb) to 0.038 wt% (0.04Nb), while all other listed elements differ by less than 0.1 wt%.
The Al (8.35 vs 8.37 wt%) and C (1.39 vs 1.33 wt%) contents of austenite, the constituents of κ-carbide, are nearly identical in the two steels.
The listed elements sum to approximately 90.7 wt% for the 0.02Nb steel and 90.8 wt% for the 0.04Nb steel, so the table does not account for the full composition.
The caption states that the table gives the quantitative chemical compositions (wt%) of austenite in the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels.
The citing text states that the chemical compositions of the austenite matrix in the as-cast Nb-containing steels were analysed using EPMA.
The citing text states that Nb is uniformly dispersed within the austenite grain, with only sporadic Nb enrichment at grain boundaries, in the Nb-containing steels.
The citing text concludes that slight variations in ferrite and NbC content have minimal impact on the chemical composition of austenite in the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels, particularly for Al and C.
The citing text states that the increased Nb content and the aging treatments have minimal impact on the constituent phase fraction and its chemical compositions, as shown in Table 4.
The citing text infers from Table 4 that the ferrite chemical composition remains almost unchanged, limiting the effect of Nb content on solid-solution strengthening in ferrite.
